risks: Moderate for patients on tiered wards if a suppressed moderate interaction causes harm; low for prescribers. Mitigated by keeping potassium-raising combinations interruptive for kidney impairment and by targeted harm surveillance with a stopping review.
consent: Prescribers are the direct participants but cannot opt out of a ward setting; they receive information and can decline alert review of their orders being used for research. Patients are affected indirectly; a waiver of patient consent is requested because the display is a system setting within usual care and individual consent is impracticable, with notices on every ward.
data: Alert logs and review forms carry order identifiers only; results are reported by arm, never by prescriber.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: older adults, people with kidney impairment and patients on many medicines carry most interaction risk; results are reported for patients aged 75 and over and for reduced kidney function. Junior doctors see more alerts and are over-represented among prescribers; their workload is monitored.
effectiveness: The trial decides whether tiering is adopted network-wide before the order set change.
efficiency: Uses vendor configuration and existing pharmacist time with sampled review.
costs: No vendor cost within the current contract; pharmacist time within the team.
partnerships: Prescriber representatives from each hospital, the medication safety committee and two patient partners from the network's patient safety panel.
rebPath: Full network REB review under ICH-GCP and Declaration of Helsinki principles, with a request for waiver of patient consent; the REB has not reviewed it yet, and randomisation waits for approval.
limitations: Contamination; reviewer unblinding; no adverse drug event outcome; six months only.
summary: Cluster trial with a patient consent waiver request, harm surveillance and an unknown REB decision.
